subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw make retained session transcripts a durable archive contract that renames `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` and removes automatic hard-deletion, or keep the current retention model with clearer wording?
rationale: The code can implement either path, but the choice changes user storage guarantees, cleanup behavior, config semantics, and compatibility for existing archives and downstream tools.

options.title: Adopt durable archive semantics
options.body: Rename future retained transcripts to archive-oriented names or locations, migrate existing suffixes with doctor, and require explicit purge semantics for any physical deletion.

options.title: Keep current retention semantics
options.body: Leave `.deleted.*` and automatic cleanup in place, but document that the suffix means detached/retained until retention or disk budget removes it.

options.title: Split visible and physical retention
options.body: Keep archive files but introduce separate visible-session and retained-transcript retention controls with a documented migration path.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable archive semantics
recommendation.body: Rename future retained transcripts to archive-oriented names or locations, migrate existing suffixes with doctor, and require explicit purge semantics for any physical deletion.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session product work makes this the best available owner for the product-level transcript lifecycle choice, with cleanup implementation details likely shared with archive-maintenance contributors.
